title: Reliability activation playbook for edge model serving
content:
Quick summary:
This is a cross-functional activation playbook for operationalizing SLOs, runbooks, and staffing for ‘edge model serving’ — a new distribution of Redwood inference nodes we expect to deploy at partner edge sites and lightweight VPCs. Purpose is to define minimal reliability guarantees, handoffs, and experiments to validate SLO assumptions before we scale. This doc mixes concrete tasks, decision checkpoints, and a risk-first approach (we expect many unknowns).

Goals (what success looks like in 60 days):
- Define 3 measurable SLOs for edge-serving pilot (availability, cold-start latency, and correctness/regression rate) with data sources and owners.
- Complete one controlled pilot across 2 partner regions with automated telemetry, a canary routing policy, and documented rollback criteria.
- Produce and rehearse an on-call runbook covering the top-6 failure modes for edge nodes.
- Staff a lightweight operational cadence (weekly readout + daily check-in during pilot launch window).

Context / why this is different:
Edge-serving means: intermittent WAN links, less homogeneous GPUs/accelerators, small bursty workloads, higher variance in request batching, and stronger constraints on persistent KV caches. These constraints change our usual assumptions about SLO thresholds and mitigations (e.g., prefix cache effectiveness is lower; network fallback is more common). We need SRE, serving-runtime, platform-engineering, product-hosted-api, and solutions-engineering to align before rollout.

Key stakeholders and roles (RACI-lite):
- Product lead (edge-serving): Jenna Li — defines product acceptance and business risk.
- Serving runtime lead: Marco Ruiz — implements runtime toggles (graceful degradation, model-variant routing).
- Platform & infra: Omar Haddad — manages provisioning, node health checks, and autoscaling policies for edge pools.
- SRE / Reliability: Aisha Patel (owner) — defines SLOs, runbooks, incident playbooks, and coordinates drills.
- Console & Observability: Priya Nair — dashboards, trace hooks, synthetic checks.
- Customer Success / Solutions Eng: Assigned AE for partner pilot — coordinates partner ops and test windows.

Proposed SLOs (draft values — finalize after bench runs):
1) Availability (successful response within system timeout): 99.5% per region per week. Measurement: platform health pings + synthetic request success. Owner: Platform & SRE.
2) Cold-start tail latency (95th percentile for first token after cold connection): <= 400ms. Measurement: per-request metadata flagging cold starts, traces exported to tracing backend. Owner: Serving runtime.
3) Quality regression (semantic correctness vs canary baseline): <= 1.5% regression rate per release. Measurement: pre-defined evaluation prompts bubbled from QA suite and automated eval infra. Owner: Product + Research/Applied ML.

Notes: these are conservative for pilot. If we see stable results, we will tighten to hosted-L1 parity targets. Also create a fall-through SLO for graceful-degradation responses (e.g., reduced model-size fallback) to reflect intentional degradations rather than failures.

Telemetry and observability plan (minimum viable):
- Edge node exporter metrics (cpu/gpu, mem, kv-cache hit rate, queue length, last-heartbeat).
- Synthetic pings from partner region every 30s with full request/response trace retained for 90d.
- Prefix/KV cache hit/miss emitted per inference request.
- Cold-start flag and first-token-timestamp per session.
- Sampling of text outputs (privacy scrubbed) for quality-check evals.
- Alerting: platform-health (node down >3m), latency-exceeding (p95 cold-start >500ms for 5m), regression-alert (automated eval surpasses threshold). Owner: Priya Nair + SRE.

Runbook skeleton (top failure modes + immediate mitigations):
1) Node unreachable / network partition
  - Detection: missed heartbeats + synthetic ping failures.
  - Immediate actions: switch traffic via canary routing policy to alternate region/hosted fallback; open incident channel; escalate to platform.
  - Long-term: add circuit-breaker that degrades to smaller model variant/policy after 3 consecutive pings fail.

2) Persistent cold-start tail spikes
  - Detection: sustained p95 cold-start >400ms for 15m.
  - Immediate actions: enable pre-warm pool for hot models, increase prefetching of KV state, temporary route low-priority traffic to hosted.
  - Long-term: measure warming success rates and refine kernel selection on heterogenous HW.

3) Model quality regression after push
  - Detection: automated eval cohort fails regression threshold.
  - Immediate actions: rollback to previous model version, run targeted eval subset to scope failure. Product to own customer comms.

4) KV cache corruption or desync
  - Detection: sudden drop in cache hit rate with increased backend load.
  - Immediate actions: flush local KV cache, fail-safe to fetch state from central store, patch instrumentation to capture last-good-state.

5) Thundering-burst overload (small supply of nodes)
  - Detection: queue-length growth + high token-cost rate per node.
  - Immediate actions: spike autoscale (if configured), enable batching relaxation knob (if safe), shift non-critical traffic to hosted.

6) Data compliance or PII exposure alert from partner
  - Detection: automated scrub failure or partner-reported exposure.
  - Immediate actions: pause data sampling, engage security/compliance, rotate keys if necessary.

Launch & experiment plan (8-week cadence broken into sprint-like checkpoints):
- Week 0–1: Bench & baseline
  - Run model-runtime bench on representative edge hardware. Capture cold-warm latency curves, KV behavioral matrix.
  - Deliverable: bench report + recommended default runtime knobs.
- Week 2: Observability wiring
  - Enable exporters, set up synthetic pings, create dashboards for SLOs.
  - Deliverable: live dashboard with baseline metrics.
- Week 3: Canary + small partner trial (region A)
  - Route 5% traffic to edge pilot. Enable canary rollback. Begin daily readouts.
- Week 4: Failover rehearsal + runbook drill
  - Simulate node-network partition, verify automatic reroute and SRE playbook steps.
- Week 5: Quality sweep + model-eval
  - Run full automated eval on production-like prompts. Check regression metric.
- Week 6: Expand to region B (if stability targets met)
- Week 7–8: Stabilize and document operational handbook; prepare handoff to ongoing operations and scale plan.

Staffing & operational cadence:
- Launch week: 24/7 on-call coverage for platform + serving-runtime (rotating, 4 engineers) for first 72h of canary.
- Daily pilot standup (15m) during canary window. Weekly sync with partner and product.
- Post-pilot triage + decision on SLO tightening after 14 days of stable telemetry.

Decision gates (must-pass to expand):
- Gate 1 (canary enable): synthetic success rate >99% for 48h, no regressions in eval cohort.
- Gate 2 (region expansion): p95 cold-start <400ms and availability >=99.5% for 7 consecutive days.
- Gate 3 (scale): capacity card and cost projection validated by finance for sustained traffic.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- We need to finalize exact metric names for platform telemetry vs runtime telemetry (avoid conflicting labels). Action: Priya to propose naming conventions by 2026-06-19.
- How aggressive should fallback policies be for partners with SLA constraints? Product to provide partner tiers and allowed degradations.
- Privacy: sampling frequency for output traces — legal signoff required. Add to partner contract template.

Risk register (top risks + mitigations):
- Risk: Intermittent connectivity causes higher perceived downtime for customers. Mitigation: make invisible fallback to hosted with clear SLA notes and telemetry tag for degraded response.
- Risk: Edge nodes use mixed accelerator drivers causing runtime errors. Mitigation: enforce compatibility matrix and preflight checks in provisioning flow.
- Risk: Over-collection of sampled outputs causes partner privacy concern. Mitigation: default off; opt-in reporting; scrub pipeline.

Communication plan:
- Internal: daily pilot standup + Slack channel #edge-pilot and a binder with runbook pinned.
- External (partners): pre-launch call + weekly readouts; immediate incident comms if availability <99% in a 1h window.

Artifacts to produce (deliverables):
- Bench report (platform + runtime)
- SLO dashboard and alert ruleset
- Edge runbook (detailed step-by-step)
- Post-pilot lessons-learned and decision memo

Appendix: quick checklist for readiness (pre-canary):
- [ ] Telemetry exporters live and dashboard emits baseline
- [ ] Canary routing policy implemented with rollback flag
- [ ] Autoscaling policy for pilot thresholds
- [ ] Pre-warm pool available for top-2 models
- [ ] Legal/compliance signoff on sampling policy
- [ ] On-call rota confirmed for launch week

If you’re reading this as an owner: please add comments inline and tag who will own each checklist item. This is intentionally a pragmatic, low-bureaucracy playbook — we will evolve it into the canonical SLO program docs if pilot succeeds.

- Confluence: EDGE-SERVING-READOUT-2026 (archival bench and trial notes)
